fields.features_heading: What the App Does With Each Questionnaire
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the answer library and the review steps as one app from your prompt, with the data in a database you own.
fields.feature_1:
Each questionnaire read into rows

Upload the buyer's spreadsheet or document, and the app reads it into one row per question with AI. A question it cannot read cleanly goes to a person before matching starts.
fields.feature_2:
An answer library your team approved

Every answer in the library carries the name of the person who approved it and the date. The app checks each new question against the library before anyone on the team is asked.
fields.feature_3:
Open questions go to the topic owner

You map topics to people once, such as backups to infrastructure and background checks to HR. A question with no approved answer goes straight to that owner with a due date.
fields.feature_4:
Reminders before a deadline slips

Owners get a Slack or email reminder on the due date, and a second one the day after. You choose how many days late an answer can run before the security lead is copied in.
fields.feature_5:
Questionnaire status on the CRM deal

The app writes each questionnaire's status to the deal in HubSpot or any CRM with an API. Account executives read the deal record instead of asking security for an update.
fields.feature_6:
No cap when questionnaires pile up

Run every questionnaire a quarter brings with no task cap, and add reviewers with no per-approver seats. On a paid plan, export the app's full code to your GitHub repository.

fields.usecase_heading: Where a Questionnaire Goes After It Arrives
fields.tab_content_1:
A 140-question spreadsheet leaves 22 for people

Merriwell Health sends Quellbrook Analytics a 140-question security questionnaire as a spreadsheet. The app reads it into 140 questions and finds an approved answer in the library for 118 of them. The other 22 stay open, and each goes to the owner of its topic.
fields.tab_content_2:
Backup questions reach one owner with 2 days to answer

Nine open questions cover backups and hosting and go to the infrastructure lead, Ilse Varga, due in 2 days. She answers 7 by the due date. The 2 still open get a Slack reminder, and a day later the security lead, Teodor Amsel, is copied in.
fields.tab_content_3:
The security lead approves 20 answers and returns 2

Nothing goes back to Merriwell Health until Teodor Amsel reviews the 22 new answers. He approves 20 and returns 2 to their owners with a comment. Each approved answer is saved to the library with his name and the date, ready for the next questionnaire.
fields.tab_content_4:
Each open questionnaire shows on its deal in HubSpot

Quellbrook's sales team has 6 questionnaires open, listed on the dashboard by due date. Merriwell Health's is due in 3 days and sits at In review. The account executive, Callum Ferreira, sees that status on his HubSpot deal without asking security.

fields.howto_description: Follow these seven steps to build an answer library from past replies and launch security questionnaire automation that routes the rest.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Approve a first set of answers
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Describe the flow in a prompt
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pull every questionnaire your team answered in the past year, along with the files you sent with them. Note which buyer sent each one and how many days the reply took. The questions that repeat show what the library needs first.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write one answer for each question that came up in three or more questionnaires. Have the security lead approve every answer before it enters the library, and record who approved it and on which date.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Assign each topic, such as background checks or vendor management, to one named person. Add a second person for the weeks the first is out, because a shared inbox cannot be reminded.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Describe the flow the way you would brief a new security analyst, starting with the file that arrives and ending with the sign-off. Emergent builds the app from that description.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Connect your CRM and Slack through their APIs, such as HubSpot. Each questionnaire then sits on its deal, and owners get reminders in the tool they already check.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Before going live, run one questionnaire you have already answered through the app. Compare its matches with the replies you sent, and fix any rule by prompting until the two agree.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Put a review date on every answer
fields.howto_step_7_des: Give each library answer a review date, such as 6 months after approval. An answer past that date goes back to its owner to confirm before the app reuses it.
fields.hero_prompt: Build security questionnaire automation that runs on its own and logs every step.

faq_plan.a: A security questionnaire is a standardized document or set of questions that organizations send to vendors during the procurement or vendor evaluation process. The buyer checks that your data protection policies and risk posture meet its requirements. Security questionnaire automation reuses replies your team has already approved.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up security questionnaire automation?
faq_plan.a: Start with the questionnaires you answered last year and approve one answer for each repeated question. Then describe how questions should move in a prompt to Emergent's AI automation builder, and Emergent builds the app around your library. You change a rule later by prompting again, and the free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: Is best rated security questionnaire automation worth it for a small security team?
faq_plan.a: It depends on volume. Count the questionnaires your team answered last quarter and the hours each one took, and compare that with the time an answer library would save. A team that answers two a year can keep a shared document. An app built on Emergent has no task cap. A quarter with ten questionnaires runs on the same app as a quiet one.

faq_plan.q: What features does the best security questionnaire automation software need?
faq_plan.a: It needs an answer library where every answer has an owner and a review date, and a reviewer who approves new answers before they go out. Check that it imports the formats your buyers send, such as spreadsheets and documents. Keep the policies those answers cite up to date with document automation before the library quotes them.

faq_plan.q: How do top security questionnaire automation tools draft their answers?
faq_plan.a: They start from answers you have already approved. Vanta says it combs through your knowledge base of security documentation and previous questionnaires to generate responses for new questionnaires. Conveyor says its AI only pulls from your approved knowledge. Either way, a draft is only as good as the library behind it. Audit the library before you judge the drafts.

faq_plan.q: How much of a questionnaire can security questionnaire response automation answer?
faq_plan.a: It can answer every question your approved library already covers, and nothing beyond that without a person. Track the share of each questionnaire answered from the library, and add every newly approved answer so the next one starts further along. Questions that keep landing with owners point to the library entries to write next.

faq_plan.q: When in a deal does a buyer send a security questionnaire?
faq_plan.a: A buyer sends it during procurement or vendor evaluation, while it decides whether to bring you on as a vendor. Treat each questionnaire as part of the sales cycle and set its due date from the deal's expected close. If your team buys software too, you can run the same review as an approval step ahead of purchase order automation for any new vendor.

faq_plan.q: Can I build my own security questionnaire automation software instead of buying a tool?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent builds the app from a plain-English prompt, with a library of approved answers and an approval step for new ones, and the data lives in a database you own. Start with one buyer's questionnaire and the answers you have already approved, then add topic owners as new questions come in.

faq_plan.q: Which standard security questionnaire should my answer library cover first?
faq_plan.a: Cover the standard questionnaires your buyers send, starting with the one that arrived most often last year. If you sell a cloud service, map the CAIQ once. It is a survey provided by the Cloud Security Alliance for cloud consumers and auditors to assess the security capabilities of a cloud service provider. It contains a series of yes or no control-assertion questions.

faq_plan.q: Can I reuse compliance evidence in security questionnaire answers?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Point each library answer at the record that proves it, such as last quarter's access review. If you already collect that evidence with compliance automation, the questionnaire answer and the audit file rest on the same record. The app Emergent builds connects to any tool with an API, including the one that holds that record.
